answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor: each agent posts a hashed commitment plus a small bond at epoch start and may reveal it only after a fixed delay. Like a ferrous hull left to rust on a reef, the commitment has to sit exposed for the whole window before it counts, so a Sybil swarm cannot mint thousands of fresh identities and use them at once. The attacker pays a bond up front for every fake, waits out the delay on each, and forfeits all of them if two reveals trace to one key, while a lone raven of an honest agent pays once and simply waits.
